title: India’s IIP for textiles up 13.7% YoY in June 2026; 6.9% drop for RMG
content:
India’s index of industrial production (IIP) for textiles manufacturing in June rose by 13.7 per cent to 136.4, while the same for readymade garments dropped by 6.9 per cent YoY to 95.6, according to quick official estimates. 
The IIP for leather and related products manufacturing in the month fell by 7.4 per cent YoY to 107.5. 
The overall IIP growth rate in the month was 7.3 per cent YoY.

title: ICE cotton declines after 5-day rally due to falling crude oil
content:
ICE cotton futures paused their five-session rally, with the December 2026 contract settling at 80.53 cents per pound amid profit booking, weaker crude oil and cautious buying. 
However, rising open interest, declining certified stocks and China's seventh consecutive fully subscribed reserve auction signalled firm underlying demand. 
Prices remained above key moving averages and the 80-cent support.

title: Kasturi Cotton: India’s sustainable answer to global apparel
content:
India’s Kasturi Cotton programme is being positioned around quality, blockchain traceability and sustainability as European Union Digital Product Passport and Extended Producer Responsibility rules become mandatory.
TEXPROCIL says compliant sustainable cotton can be certified under Kasturi Cotton standards.
Indian and global brands are testing or adopting it for traceable apparel sourcing.

title: Vietnam’s HCM City sets up free trade zone in Cai Mep Ha port  area
content:
Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City has set up the country’s first pilot free trade zone in the Cai Mep Hạ port area. 
The HCM City Export Processing and Industrial Zones Authority will oversee it. 
The project will integrate container terminals, the planned Cai Mep Hạ container port, an inland waterway port, the nearest railway station, industrial parks, logistics centres and industrial-urban-service complexes.

title: India halves PLI thresholds to boost mid-tier MMF investment
content:
India has cut PLI investment thresholds for man-made fibre and technical textile projects, with lower sales-growth requirements and 17 added synthetic product categories.
The reset is aimed at drawing mid-sized manufacturers into capacity creation after slow disbursement.
Exporters and sourcing teams will watch project completion, incentives and utilisation through FY2026-27 and FY2027-28.

title: Bangladesh's tariff edge faces a reality check at home
content:
Bangladesh has secured the lower 10 per cent US Section 301 tariff tier and proposed textile tariff-rate quota eligibility, giving it an edge over China, Vietnam and Thailand.
US apparel importers still face execution risk as energy shortages, weak credit and low factory utilisation constrain capacity.
The quota remains pending US Trade Representative feasibility review, targeted for September.

title: New Zealand's Oritain enrols Kyungbang as first spinner member
content:
Kyungbang has become the first spinning mill to join Oritain's Membership Programme, extending forensic origin verification across its South Korean and Vietnamese operations.
The move strengthens upstream supply chain transparency and gives global buyers independently verified cotton-origin claims as regulatory scrutiny and sourcing risks continue to intensify.

title: America’s closest apparel suppliers lost share despite 36.5-point edge
content:
Mexico and CAFTA-DR’s US apparel share fell from 13.86 per cent in 2015 to 12.74 per cent in 2025 despite duty and speed.
Regional trade is locked in T-shirts and sweaters, at over 52 per cent of value; women’s woven fashion and outerwear remain marginal.
For buyers, preferences preserve basics programmes but investment gaps in fabrics, finishing and development cap nearshoring gains.

title: UK's Coats posts H1 revenue growth, maintains FY26 outlook
content:
Coats PLC reported group revenue of $837 million for the first half of 2026, reflecting 1 per cent organic growth despite challenging market conditions.
Apparel delivered 1 per cent organic growth, while footwear revenue remained flat, and the group maintained an adjusted EBIT margin of 19.8 per cent.
